correctness.rationale: Exact two-by-two rational inverse and singular incompatibility prove sign-separated pairwise feasibility; interlaced witnesses yield k+1 components. Norm-controlled finite perturbations preserve signs for complete positive interactions and open coefficient neighborhoods. Each early positive witness contains a saddle Jacobian block and all other blocks are hyperbolic. The final witness has positive-definite symmetric competition matrix, with strict relative-entropy derivative and compact positive Lyapunov level sets, proving global attraction. Exact arithmetic checker confirms representative dimensions; infinite theorem follows from proof.

value.rationale: The nearest ecological paper highlights multiple small-community feasibility reversals but observes a single typical large-random-community transition. A dimension-linear robust lower bound for densely connected strictly competitive systems shows that worst-case feasibility complexity remains unbounded despite all-to-all competition; saddle versus global-attraction witness separation makes the algebraic/nonlinear dynamical distinction ecologically meaningful. This is an intrinsically motivated extremal question, not an arbitrary parameter table.
